metadata.title: AICTE PS 26262 Critical Architecture Constraints
metadata.purpose: Supplement the detailed rules and supplementary rules with three critical architecture requirements.
metadata.important_notice: This is an implementation specification, not proof of implementation or an official AICTE rulebook. Inspect the existing repository and original architecture documents before coding.

requirements.name: Isolated Rehearsal and Crash-Test Engine
requirements.objective: Allow hypothetical application changes to be tested without mutating production data.
required_behavior: Read the production baseline without modifying it.
Create or use an isolated snapshot for each rehearsal.
Perform all rehearsal writes in the sim schema or another explicitly approved isolated simulation store.
Compute a finding-level difference between baseline and simulated results.
Return production_modified=false only when isolation has been enforced and verified for the rehearsal.
Record the rehearsal ID, baseline version, hypothetical inputs, results, findings diff, timestamps, and execution status.
Mark a rehearsal stale when its baseline changes, according to the documented versioning policy.
Keep rehearsal operations separate from ordinary production workflow transitions.
isolation_constraints: The rehearsal execution path must not insert, update, or delete production application, workflow, evidence, assignment, or decision records.
Do not rely on an implicit database search_path to enforce isolation.
Do not accept arbitrary caller-provided schema names in SQL.
Use database permissions or an equivalent enforceable boundary to prevent simulation code from writing production tables.
A transaction rollback alone is not sufficient isolation.
Never copy simulation results into production automatically.

acceptance_tests.scenario: Run a rehearsal with hypothetical application changes.
acceptance_tests.expected: Simulation results and finding-level differences are returned without production changes.

acceptance_tests.scenario: Compare production record versions or hashes before and after a rehearsal.
acceptance_tests.expected: Production application, workflow, and evidence data remain unchanged.

acceptance_tests.scenario: Attempt a rehearsal write to a production table.
acceptance_tests.expected: Database permissions or the enforced isolation boundary reject the write.

acceptance_tests.scenario: Change the production baseline after a rehearsal snapshot is created.
acceptance_tests.expected: The rehearsal is marked stale or handled according to the documented baseline-version policy.

acceptance_tests.scenario: A rehearsal fails halfway through execution.
acceptance_tests.expected: Partial simulation data is contained or cleaned up, the failure is recorded, and production data remains unchanged.

implementation_notes: Inspect existing database migrations, ORM models, schema configuration, and rehearsal services before changing anything.
Verify whether public and sim schemas already exist.
Inspect existing sim_* models and reuse them when appropriate.
Do not claim isolation is implemented until database-level or equivalent isolation tests pass.
Do not invent a Rehearsal Load Factor formula. If the architecture leaves it undefined, keep it null until its formula, units, and test matrix are approved.

requirements.name: OCR Grounding, Fuzzy Matching, and Bounding Boxes
requirements.objective: Ensure model-extracted values are supported by document evidence and preserve source locations for reviewer verification.
required_pipeline: Validate and classify the uploaded document.
Extract native PDF text when usable.
Run OCR on scanned or low-text pages when required.
Preserve OCR text, page numbers, word or span confidence, and bounding-box coordinates.
If vision-model extraction is enabled, validate its response against the configured JSON schema.
For every extracted field, identify candidate supporting OCR text on the same page.
Normalize values conservatively for comparison without overwriting the original candidate value.
Fuzzy-match the candidate value against the relevant OCR text using a documented algorithm.
If the value cannot be adequately grounded, mark it review_required or equivalent.
Persist grounding evidence, match score, algorithm version, page number, and bounding box.
Expose page and bounding-box data to the frontend for source highlighting.
Preserve earlier extraction runs when a document is replaced or reprocessed.

grounding_contract.default_matching_scope: Same document version and same page
grounding_contract.cross_page_matching: Only when an explicit field-specific rule allows it
normalization_steps: Apply punctuation normalization only when safe for the field
Apply date or identifier normalization only through explicit field-specific rules

matching_strategy.preferred_method: Token or span-aware matching with fuzzy similarity to tolerate OCR noise
matching_strategy.high_risk_policy: Generic fuzzy similarity alone must not validate high-risk fields. Require exact or field-specific normalized matching, or human review.
matching_strategy.threshold_policy: Store the threshold and algorithm version. Calibrate thresholds on labelled examples. If 0.75 is specified in the original architecture, treat it as a proposed starting point until validated.

rules: Document the coordinate origin and units.
Ensure coordinates are finite, ordered, and within page bounds.
Specify whether coordinates use PDF coordinates or rendered-image pixels.
Use consistent coordinate conversion in the frontend.
If multiple OCR tokens support a value, store a combined region or a list of token regions.
Never invent bounding-box coordinates when no reliable region is available.

failure_policy: If OCR is unavailable, mark grounding unavailable and require review where needed.
If no supporting OCR span exists, do not mark the field grounded.
If multiple matches are ambiguous, preserve candidate locations and require review when necessary.
If output is malformed or confidence is insufficient, reject it or route it to review.
If OCR, model, or provider processing fails, record the failure; never infer compliance.
When a document is replaced, create a new version and processing run while retaining prior results.

acceptance_tests.scenario: The model returns a value supported by OCR text on the same page.
acceptance_tests.expected: The value is grounded according to the configured field policy and has valid page and bounding-box provenance.

acceptance_tests.scenario: The model invents a value absent from the OCR evidence.
acceptance_tests.expected: The field is not marked grounded or verified and requires review.

acceptance_tests.scenario: A date or official identifier differs by one character.
acceptance_tests.expected: A generic fuzzy threshold cannot silently validate the value.

acceptance_tests.scenario: OCR text matches but the bounding box is missing or invalid.
acceptance_tests.expected: The system does not fabricate coordinates; the field is flagged or review is required as appropriate.

acceptance_tests.scenario: A reviewer opens a grounded field in the frontend.
acceptance_tests.expected: The correct page and supporting region are highlighted using the documented coordinate conversion.

acceptance_tests.scenario: A document is replaced and processed again.
acceptance_tests.expected: New results reference the new document version, and previous results remain auditable.

requirements.name: External LLM Guardrails and ExternalCallLog
requirements.objective: Constrain and audit external model calls so model output cannot bypass grounding, deterministic rules, or human decision authority.
required_behavior: Route external model calls through a provider adapter rather than calling providers directly from API routes or business rules.
Explicitly set temperature to 0 for the required extraction calls.
Validate every model response against a strict, versioned JSON schema before accepting it.
Reject malformed JSON, missing required fields, invalid types, unexpected fields in strict mode, and out-of-range values.
Ground extracted values against OCR evidence after schema validation.
Record model and provider metadata, prompt version, schema version, request purpose, document/version references, timestamps, duration, outcome, retries, and normalized error codes.
Provide an explicit configuration switch to enable or disable external model calls.
If the architecture requires external calls to be disabled by default, preserve that default.
Apply timeouts, bounded retries, rate and cost limits, and safe failure handling.
Do not allow model output to directly change application status, assignments, permissions, regulatory rules, or final decisions.
Minimize sensitive document data sent externally and follow approved privacy requirements.
Keep API keys and secrets out of source code and logs.

privacy_rules: Never log API keys or authorization headers.
Do not persist full document contents or full prompts and responses by default.
If detailed payload retention is approved for debugging, apply redaction, access controls, and retention limits.
Prefer protected evidence references and bounded metadata where sufficient.
Restrict access to sensitive call logs.

schema_validation_contract.unknown_or_missing_fields: Reject or route to review; do not silently coerce materially different data.
schema_validation_contract.numeric_and_date_fields: Apply field-specific type, range, and format checks.
schema_validation_contract.final_decision_fields: The extraction schema must not let a model authorize final approval or rejection.

acceptance_tests.expected: Temperature is explicitly set to 0 for the required extraction call path.

acceptance_tests.scenario: The provider returns malformed JSON or schema-invalid output.
acceptance_tests.expected: The output is rejected or marked review-required, and ExternalCallLog records the validation failure.

acceptance_tests.scenario: The provider times out, rate-limits, or becomes unavailable.
acceptance_tests.expected: Retries remain bounded, failure is logged, and no compliance pass is inferred.
No external request is sent and the operation returns a safe disabled or manual-review outcome.

acceptance_tests.scenario: The model returns schema-valid but OCR-ungrounded data.
acceptance_tests.expected: Grounding checks prevent the value from being accepted as verified.

acceptance_tests.scenario: Inspect ExternalCallLog after successful and failed calls.
acceptance_tests.expected: Required metadata and normalized outcomes are present, without secrets or unapproved raw content.

acceptance_tests.scenario: Model output attempts to approve or reject an application.
acceptance_tests.expected: The service boundary prevents the model output from performing the decision.

global_invariants.statement: A rehearsal must never mutate production application, workflow, document, evidence, assignment, or decision data.
global_invariants.verification: Database isolation tests and before/after production version or hash comparisons.

global_invariants.statement: Schema-valid model output is not verified unless grounding and field-specific validation also pass.
global_invariants.verification: Tests for invented values, OCR noise, high-risk fields, missing bounding boxes, and ambiguous matches.

global_invariants.statement: Every attempted external model call must have an auditable outcome, including failures, timeouts, schema rejections, and grounding rejections.
global_invariants.verification: Call-log tests across success and failure paths.

global_invariants.statement: OCR and LLM output may support preliminary checks but cannot make final regulatory approval or rejection decisions.

implementation_order.name: Inspect repository before coding
tasks: Inspect database schemas, migrations, ORM models, and rehearsal services.
Inspect all database sessions and write paths used by rehearsal execution.
Inspect OCR output and whether word-level bounding boxes are retained.
Inspect fuzzy_grounding.py and grounded_lease_extractor if present.
Inspect the LLM adapter, external-call switch, ExternalCallLog model, migrations, and tests.
Document existing, partial, and missing implementation before changing code.

implementation_order.name: Enforce rehearsal isolation
tasks: Verify or implement enforceable separation between production and simulation writes.
Verify or implement finding-level diff output.
Ensure production_modified is derived from verified behavior, not hardcoded.
Add isolation and failure-path tests.

implementation_order.name: Implement OCR grounding and bounding boxes
tasks: Verify or implement token/span matching with field-specific high-risk rules.
Persist page and bounding-box provenance with explicit coordinate conventions.
Expose source-region highlighting to the frontend.
Add hallucinated-value, OCR-noise, and bounding-box tests.

implementation_order.name: Harden external LLM integration
tasks: Verify or implement provider-adapter-only calls.
Set temperature to 0 for the required extraction path.
Validate responses against strict versioned JSON schemas.
Verify or implement ExternalCallLog and the external-call enable/disable switch.
Add timeout, bounded retry, privacy-safe logging, schema rejection, and grounding rejection tests.

implementation_order.name: Verify end-to-end behavior
tasks: Run targeted tests for all three architecture requirements.
Run the relevant full test suite.
Record test results, skipped tests, environment limitations, and remaining gaps.
Update requirement traceability without claiming unverified behavior is complete.

agent_instructions: Read the original PRD, architecture, scaffold, detailed rules JSON, supplementary rules JSON, and this file before editing.
Inspect the current repository before creating duplicate models, services, migrations, schemas, or endpoints.
Do not weaken database isolation, OCR grounding, schema validation, external-call logging, or human decision authority to make tests pass.
Do not claim a requirement is implemented until code inspection and acceptance tests prove it.
Report files changed, database/API changes, tests run, skipped tests, and unresolved risks.
If an original document conflicts with this specification, identify the conflict explicitly rather than silently choosing one.
